sections.subtitle: Demonstrative Determiners
sections.content:
👉 Indicate Proximity

Near speaker (this/these):
• este/esta/estos/estas
  → este libro (this book)
  → estas casas (these houses)

Medium distance (that/those):
• ese/esa/esos/esas
  → esa casa (that house)
  → esos días (those days)

Far from both (that/those - far):
• aquel/aquella/aquellos/aquellas
  → aquellos días (those days)
  → aquella montaña (that mountain)

✅ Agree in gender & number with noun

sections.subtitle: Possessive Determiners
sections.content:
🤝 Show Ownership

Always BEFORE the noun:

• mi/mis → my
• tu/tus → your (informal)
• su/sus → his/her/your (formal)/their
• nuestro/nuestra/nuestros/nuestras → our
• vuestro/vuestra/vuestros/vuestras → your (plural, Spain)

Examples:
• mi libro (my book)
• mis libros (my books)
• nuestra casa (our house)
• nuestras casas (our houses)

⚠️ Agree with POSSESSED ITEM, not possessor

sections.subtitle: Quantifiers: Expressing Amount
sections.content:
🔢 How Much/How Many

Much/Many:
• mucho/mucha/muchos/muchas
  → mucho dinero (much money)
  → muchas personas (many people)

Little/Few:
• poco/poca/pocos/pocas
  → poco tiempo (little time)
  → pocos libros (few books)

Several:
• varios/varias
  → varias opciones (several options)

Too much/many:
• demasiado/demasiada/demasiados/demasiadas
  → demasiado trabajo (too much work)

Enough/Quite a lot:
• bastante/bastantes
  → bastante comida (enough food)

✅ All agree with the noun

sections.subtitle: Indefinite Determiners
sections.content:
❓ Non-specific Items

Some/Any (positive):
• algún/alguna/algunos/algunas
  → algún día (some day)
  → algunas personas (some people)

No/None/Any (negative):
• ningún/ninguna
  → ningún problema (no problem)
  → ninguna razón (no reason)

Any (choice):
• cualquier/cualesquiera
  → cualquier día (any day)

⚠️ Apocopation before masc. singular:
• alguno → algún
• ninguno → ningún

💡 Double negative in Spanish:
• No tengo ningún libro
  → I don't have any book

sections.subtitle: Distributive Determiners
sections.content:
📊 Each/Every/All

Each/Every (invariable):
• cada + singular noun
  → cada día (each/every day)
  → cada persona (each person)

All/Every/Whole:
• todo/toda/todos/todas

Different meanings:
• todo el día → all day long (whole)
• toda la casa → the whole house
• todos los días → every day (habitual)
• todas las personas → all people

Both (always plural):
• ambos/ambas
  → ambos libros (both books)
  → ambas manos (both hands)

sections.subtitle: Key Differences & Usage
sections.content:
💡 Important Rules

❌ NO possessives with articles:
• mi casa ✅
• la mi casa ❌
• tu libro ✅
• el tu libro ❌

🔄 Determiners → Pronouns:

Demonstratives:
• este libro (this book) → este (this one)
• esa casa (that house) → esa (that one)

Quantifiers:
• muchos libros (many books) → muchos (many)
• pocos estudiantes (few students) → pocos (few)

✅ Determiners are more specific than articles
→ They give more information about the noun

questions.question: Which demonstrative means 'this' (masculine singular)?
questions.hint: This is the nearest demonstrative for masculine singular nouns.

questions.question: Which demonstrative means 'these' (feminine)?
questions.hint: Plural form of 'esta' (this). Used for nearby feminine plural nouns.

questions.question: Which demonstrative indicates medium distance (masculine)?
questions.hint: This means 'that' for items near the listener but not the speaker.

questions.question: Which demonstrative indicates far distance (feminine plural)?
questions.hint: This means 'those' for items far from both speaker and listener (feminine).

questions.question: What is the possessive determiner for 'my' (plural)?
questions.hint: Add -s to 'mi' when the possessed item is plural: mis libros (my books).

questions.question: What is the possessive for 'our' with a masculine singular noun?
questions.hint: 'Our' in Spanish changes form. Use the masculine singular form here.

questions.question: Which possessive is ambiguous (can mean his/her/their/your formal)?
questions.hint: This possessive has multiple meanings - context determines which one.

questions.question: How do you say 'many books' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Libros is masculine plural, so use the masculine plural form of 'mucho'.

questions.question: How do you say 'much money' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Dinero is masculine singular, so use the masculine singular form of 'mucho'.

questions.question: What does 'pocos libros' mean?
questions.hint: 'Poco' means 'little' or 'few' - the opposite of 'mucho'.

questions.question: What does 'varias personas' mean?
questions.hint: 'Varios/varias' means 'several' or 'various'. Personas is feminine plural.

questions.question: What does 'demasiado dinero' mean?
questions.hint: 'Demasiado' means 'too much' or 'too many' - excessive amount.

questions.question: What is the shortened form of 'alguno' before a masculine singular noun?
questions.hint: Drop the -o and add an accent. Example: algún día (some day).

questions.question: What is the shortened form of 'ninguno' before a masculine singular noun?
questions.hint: Drop the -o and add an accent. Example: ningún problema (no problem).

questions.question: What does 'No tengo ningún libro' mean?
questions.hint: Spanish uses double negative. 'No' + 'ningún' = negative statement.

questions.question: What does 'cada día' mean?
questions.hint: 'Cada' means 'each' or 'every' and is invariable (doesn't change form).

questions.question: What does 'todo el día' mean?

answers.text: all day long / the whole day

questions.hint: 'Todo' + article + singular noun means 'the whole' or 'all of'.

questions.question: What does 'todos los días' mean?
questions.hint: 'Todos' + article + plural noun means 'every' (habitual action).

questions.question: What does 'ambos libros' mean?
questions.hint: 'Ambos/ambas' means 'both' and is always plural.

questions.question: Which is INCORRECT in Spanish?
questions.hint: You cannot combine articles with possessive determiners in Spanish. Use one or the other, not both.
